newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: First Austrian troops leave for Albania.
newsitem.headline: First Austrian troops leave for Albania.

text.p: The first Austrian troops to join an Italian-led international security force in Albania left for the troubled Balkan nation from their barracks just outside Vienna on Wednesday.
The 74 soldiers, part of Austria's 115-strong contribution to the mission, will travel by train to the Italian port of Brindisi, where they will board a ferry to the Albanian port of Durres.
The troops will be stationed in Tirana where they will be responsible for protecting the headquarters of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
The exact location of the OSCE's headquarters had not yet been decided, commanding officer Heinz Assmann told reporters. "It will be either in a school or in a villa in downtown Tirana," he said.
The Austrian contingent includes 13 all-terrain trucks. The troops are lightly armed.

About 4,000 soldiers of the 6,000-strong international force have so far arrived in Albania. Italy, Greece, France, Spain, Romania, Turkey and Denmark are also contributing to the U.N.-backed mission, codenamed Alba (Dawn).
